title: Kth Largest Element: A Judge's Two-Seat Shortlist
summary: A min-heap capped at k keeps the k best scores; its root, the weakest of them, is the kth largest.

analogy.scenario: A talent-show judge hears scores one at a time and keeps a shortlist of the 2 best. The weakest shortlisted score is always on top of the pile, ready to be dropped.

mapping.real: The weakest shortlisted score, on top
Dropping the weakest when a third arrives
mapping.abstract: Popping the root when size > k

takeaway.summary: Push each value; whenever the heap holds k + 1, pop the root. The heap always holds the k largest so far, and its root is the kth largest.
whenToUse: The kth largest or the k largest of many values
Streams where you can't keep everything

scenes.narration: Six contestants score 7, 2, 9, 4, 9, and 1. Which score is the second best? A judge keeps a shortlist of two seats as the scores come in.
scenes.caption: Which score is 2nd best? A judge keeps a 2-seat shortlist

scenes.narration: Sorting all the scores works, but it orders everyone, even contestants who could never be in the top two.
scenes.caption: Sorting every score just to read one is more than needed

scenes.narration: Keep the shortlist in a min-heap. After 7, the score 2 arrives and sifts up to the root: the weakest seat is always on top. Both seats are full.
scenes.caption: A min-heap puts the weakest shortlisted score on top

scenes.narration: A 9 arrives, making three. Pop the root: 2 is the weakest of the three, so it can't be in the top two.
scenes.caption: 9 arrives: three is one too many, so the root 2 leaves

scenes.narration: A 4 arrives. It's weaker than both shortlisted scores, so it sifts to the root and is popped straight back out.
scenes.caption: 4 is weaker than both seats: it's dropped right away

scenes.narration: Another 9 arrives. Now 7 is the weakest of the three, so the root, 7, leaves. Both seats hold a 9.
scenes.caption: Another 9 pushes out the 7

scenes.narration: The 1 is dropped at once too. The shortlist holds the two best scores, and its root, 9, is the second best.
scenes.caption: After every score, the root is the 2nd best: 9

scenes.narration: Scores are values, the shortlist is a min-heap capped at k, and its root is the kth largest. Each value costs O(log k): O(n log k) in all.
scenes.caption: Scores are values; the shortlist is a size-k min-heap
